{
  "IP": "neorv32_cache",
  "Conceptual Assets": [
    {
      "Concept ID": "C1",
      "Concept Name": "Cache access target and direction",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Information": "The address and read/write direction identify the memory operation that the cache must look up, refill, or forward. The operation enters through the host request and can leave through the backing-bus request.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "no",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Integrity is at risk because the RTL uses the address and direction to select cache lines and construct backing-bus requests at lines 171, 180-181, and 225-239, so alteration can redirect or change an access.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I"
      ],
      "Attack": "Tamper with the address or read/write direction so a request returns data from or writes data to an unintended memory location.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "host_req_i.addr",
        "host_req_i.rw"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "bus_req_o.addr",
        "bus_req_o.rw"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        149,
        159,
        180,
        181
      ],
      "Held Lines": [],
      "Exit Lines": [
        159,
        227,
        228,
        238,
        239
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C2",
      "Concept Name": "Cache bypass and routing decision",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Information": "This decision determines whether an access uses the cache or bypasses it for a direct backing-bus transaction, including the uncached, atomic, and debug cases. It is computed and held internally and has no boundary port carrying the decision itself; it only controls other paths.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "yes"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Integrity is at risk because buf_dir is set from address, AMO, and debug conditions and selects the direct path at lines 171-188; availability is at risk because the same decision gates whether the backing bus or cache path is used at lines 186-203; the debug/bypass behavior acts directly on this decision at lines 171-175 and can therefore produce incorrect normal-operation behavior.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "Spoof the debug or atomic qualification, or corrupt the stored routing decision, to bypass the cache and force an unintended or unavailable backing-bus path.",
      "Enters Through": [],
      "Leaves Through": [],
      "Entry Lines": [],
      "Held Lines": [
        126,
        140,
        173
      ],
      "Exit Lines": []
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C3",
      "Concept Name": "Cache hit decision",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Information": "The hit decision says whether the requested line is present and selects a direct cached response versus a backing-memory access. It is generated inside the cache-memory instance and has no unit port carrying the decision itself.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "yes",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Confidentiality is at risk because the hit result changes observable response and bus timing, with direct acknowledgement at line 191 versus bus activity at lines 195 and 202; integrity is at risk because the hit selects cached data or a refill path at lines 189-203; availability is at risk because forcing misses or hits can make the operation depend on an unavailable or stalled backing bus.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "C",
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "Alter the valid/tag comparison or its hand-off so false hits return stale data, false misses trigger unnecessary refills, or hit timing reveals cache occupancy.",
      "Enters Through": [],
      "Leaves Through": [],
      "Entry Lines": [],
      "Held Lines": [
        286,
        405
      ],
      "Exit Lines": []
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C4",
      "Concept Name": "Cache flush and fence command",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Information": "A host fence request causes the cache to be cleared and, when writable, propagates a fence to the backing bus. Cache-coherence and subsequent access behavior depend on this command being retained and serviced.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Integrity is at risk because the retained fence command drives cache clearing at line 219 and a backing-bus fence at line 217, so suppressing or fabricating it can leave stale state or discard required state; availability is at risk because the command diverts the controller into S_CLEAR and can withhold normal transfers at lines 168-221.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "Inject, suppress, or repeatedly retain a fence request to clear valid cache contents or prevent normal accesses from proceeding.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "host_req_i.fence"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "bus_req_o.fence"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        138
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        126,
        138,
        219
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        217
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C5",
      "Concept Name": "Write-byte selection",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Information": "The byte-enable information determines which bytes of a cached or forwarded write are modified. It enters with the host request and is also forwarded on the backing-bus request.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "no",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Integrity is at risk because the write mask is used to form cache_o.we and determine which cached bytes are written at line 194, while it is forwarded on the bus at line 159, so changing it can corrupt or incompletely update a word.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I"
      ],
      "Attack": "Modify the byte-enable mask so a write changes unintended bytes or silently omits bytes that the requester intended to update.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "host_req_i.ben"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "bus_req_o.ben"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        159,
        194
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        194
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        159
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C6",
      "Concept Name": "Cache-line fill control",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Information": "This internal command commits a downloaded line as a new cache line and controls the transition from refill to subsequent lookup. It is generated inside the controller and sent only to the cache-memory instance, so it has no unit boundary entry or exit.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Integrity is at risk because cmd_new controls creation of valid/tag state during a refill at lines 226 and 285, so altering it can associate incorrect contents with a line; availability is at risk because suppressing the fill command can leave misses unresolved and cause repeated or stalled refills.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "Suppress or fabricate the new-line command so invalid or incomplete refill data is treated as valid, or so every access repeatedly misses.",
      "Enters Through": [],
      "Leaves Through": [],
      "Entry Lines": [],
      "Held Lines": [
        226,
        285
      ],
      "Exit Lines": []
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C7",
      "Concept Name": "Backing-bus error status",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Information": "The backing-bus error indication is accumulated during a line download, returned to the host, and used to invalidate a failed fill. Cache correctness and the host's view of transaction success depend on it.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Integrity is at risk because bus_rsp_i.err is accumulated into buf_err and reported as host_rsp_o.err at lines 242 and 257, so changing it can make failed operations appear successful or successful ones fail; availability is at risk because the error status causes invalidation and an error response at lines 254-258.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "Forge or suppress the bus error indication to accept corrupted refill data, invalidate good data, or make the host retry and lose service.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "bus_rsp_i.err"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "host_rsp_o.err"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        209,
        242
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        126,
        242
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        209,
        257
      ]
    }
  ],
  "Not Kept": [
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Relayed request and response data",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "Forwarded-transactions rules bar data that only moves between host and backing-bus ports or through the cache instance without this unit computing from it."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Cached data words, tags, and valid bits",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "Cached-copies rules treat the data as backing-memory copies and tags and valid bits as records of those copies, not as information stored by this unit."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Controller sequencing state and pending request strobe",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "Sequencing-state and bus-handshake-copy rules fold ctrl.state and buf_req into the transfer steps they pace rather than keeping them as concepts of their own."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Address staging fields",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Merged Into": "C1",
      "Why Not Kept": ""
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Build-time cache geometry and read-only setting",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "NUM_BLOCKS, BLOCK_SIZE, UC_BEGIN, and READ_ONLY are generics that fix construction or behavior at build time and cannot be changed or withheld at run time."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Clock and reset",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The clock and reset only time or reset controller and cache-memory state, and the clock/reset rules exclude them as conceptual assets."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Bus acknowledge and request handshake",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "Forwarded-transaction and bus-handshake rules treat acknowledge, strobe, and other transfer-timing copies as part of the relayed transaction rather than independent information."
    }
  ],
  "Notes": []
}

conceptual assets.information: The address and read/write direction identify the memory operation that the cache must look up, refill, or forward. The operation enters through the host request and can leave through the backing-bus request.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the RTL uses the address and direction to select cache lines and construct backing-bus requests at lines 171, 180-181, and 225-239, so alteration can redirect or change an access.
conceptual assets.attack: Tamper with the address or read/write direction so a request returns data from or writes data to an unintended memory location.

conceptual assets.information: This decision determines whether an access uses the cache or bypasses it for a direct backing-bus transaction, including the uncached, atomic, and debug cases. It is computed and held internally and has no boundary port carrying the decision itself; it only controls other paths.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because buf_dir is set from address, AMO, and debug conditions and selects the direct path at lines 171-188; availability is at risk because the same decision gates whether the backing bus or cache path is used at lines 186-203; the debug/bypass behavior acts directly on this decision at lines 171-175 and can therefore produce incorrect normal-operation behavior.
conceptual assets.attack: Spoof the debug or atomic qualification, or corrupt the stored routing decision, to bypass the cache and force an unintended or unavailable backing-bus path.

conceptual assets.information: The hit decision says whether the requested line is present and selects a direct cached response versus a backing-memory access. It is generated inside the cache-memory instance and has no unit port carrying the decision itself.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because the hit result changes observable response and bus timing, with direct acknowledgement at line 191 versus bus activity at lines 195 and 202; integrity is at risk because the hit selects cached data or a refill path at lines 189-203; availability is at risk because forcing misses or hits can make the operation depend on an unavailable or stalled backing bus.
conceptual assets.attack: Alter the valid/tag comparison or its hand-off so false hits return stale data, false misses trigger unnecessary refills, or hit timing reveals cache occupancy.

conceptual assets.information: A host fence request causes the cache to be cleared and, when writable, propagates a fence to the backing bus. Cache-coherence and subsequent access behavior depend on this command being retained and serviced.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the retained fence command drives cache clearing at line 219 and a backing-bus fence at line 217, so suppressing or fabricating it can leave stale state or discard required state; availability is at risk because the command diverts the controller into S_CLEAR and can withhold normal transfers at lines 168-221.
conceptual assets.attack: Inject, suppress, or repeatedly retain a fence request to clear valid cache contents or prevent normal accesses from proceeding.

conceptual assets.information: The byte-enable information determines which bytes of a cached or forwarded write are modified. It enters with the host request and is also forwarded on the backing-bus request.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the write mask is used to form cache_o.we and determine which cached bytes are written at line 194, while it is forwarded on the bus at line 159, so changing it can corrupt or incompletely update a word.
conceptual assets.attack: Modify the byte-enable mask so a write changes unintended bytes or silently omits bytes that the requester intended to update.

conceptual assets.information: This internal command commits a downloaded line as a new cache line and controls the transition from refill to subsequent lookup. It is generated inside the controller and sent only to the cache-memory instance, so it has no unit boundary entry or exit.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because cmd_new controls creation of valid/tag state during a refill at lines 226 and 285, so altering it can associate incorrect contents with a line; availability is at risk because suppressing the fill command can leave misses unresolved and cause repeated or stalled refills.
conceptual assets.attack: Suppress or fabricate the new-line command so invalid or incomplete refill data is treated as valid, or so every access repeatedly misses.

conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because bus_rsp_i.err is accumulated into buf_err and reported as host_rsp_o.err at lines 242 and 257, so changing it can make failed operations appear successful or successful ones fail; availability is at risk because the error status causes invalidation and an error response at lines 254-258.
